subject: Durable Execution — Provider Result Handoff & Missed-Event Recovery

diagnosis.statement: The canonical Provider Host and persistent runtime correctly materialize, bind, deduplicate, and consume transitions once a ProviderInput/event exists. The R1 interruption occurred earlier: valid result evidence persisted in Waterfound/FAE-testnet had no autonomous registered adapter/observer that transformed the workstream-owned result into General-Execution ProviderInput/event materialization.
diagnosis.first_observable_systemic_divergence: FAE R1 provider result persisted at commit 6181e3d015c40d5075269b3d5fb43fb6442e2901 while the durable manifest remained bound to the prior authority-reconciliation event at generation 7.
diagnosis.root_cause_scope: orchestration handoff only; no claim is made about the ASIC technical root cause

contributing_factors: Provider Host activation was ingress-driven from General-Execution/provider input rather than cross-repository result discovery.
No generic Build Colony/workstream completion-result adapter was registered for the FAE R1 result path.
Continuity Check is intentionally read-only and could identify CHECKPOINTED_RESUMABLE without emitting an execution transition.
The earlier FAE missed-event pilot proved recovery only after evidence had been materialized into General Execution.
A terminal verifier also contained a stale live-state assertion; this was verifier drift, not the cause of the R1 handoff silence.

hardening: Deterministic workstream-result -> ProviderInput adapter with exact repository/ref/path/schema/source-revision binding.
Explicit completion classes including NEXT_FRONTIER_DISPATCHED, wait/gate classes, DI_REQUIRED, FAILED, DONE_TECHNICAL and DONE_CANONICAL.
Existing-authority continuation requires authority evidence already present in durable state and never creates a new authority grant.
Scheduled registered-source reconciliation reuses the existing Provider Host and persistent runtime rather than creating a new orchestration brain.
Stable evidence handoff identity, state-bound runtime event identity, processed marker deduplication and runtime-head CAS.
Historical FAE R1 replay watch remains disabled for live reconciliation.

before_behavior.condition: workstream evidence persisted + admissible next + existing authority
before_behavior.possible_outcome: No ProviderInput/event materialized; durable state could remain silent until a new human/chat stimulus caused reconciliation.

after_behavior.scope: registered enabled GitHub workstream-result watches supported by the reconciler
after_behavior.condition: valid bound result + explicit disposition contract + admissible policy transition + required existing authority present
after_behavior.outcome: A deterministic ProviderInput and state-bound persistent-runtime transition are materialized; the result converges to an explicit transition class instead of silent persistence.
after_behavior.retry_semantics: If evidence discovery occurs but remote runtime commit does not complete, no processed marker is committed and a subsequent reconciliation retries deterministically. Duplicate delivery is idempotent; concurrent runtime movement is protected by runtime-head CAS.

regression_and_adversarial_evidence.case: runtime generation change rebinds event identity
result commit change changes handoff identity
persistent-runtime end-to-end consumption without human prompt

residual_risks: Evidence that exists only in an unregistered provider or workstream source cannot be discovered until an adapter/watch is registered.
The no-credential GitHub reconciler currently targets registered public GitHub result sources; private sources require explicitly authorized read access.
Provider-only storage still needs the appropriate provider-specific observer before it can enter this generic handoff path.
Polling recovery is bounded by the reconciliation cadence rather than instantaneous webhook delivery.
